business_question: Can the foundations of machine learning -- probability, evaluation, gradient descent and backpropagation -- be taught on real data, with every mechanism checked?

phases.name: business_understanding
phases.title: 1. Business Understanding
phases.objective: Teach four foundations interactively, each on a real dataset and verified against a reference.
phases.narrative: Foundations are usually taught on toy numbers, so the lessons never meet the problems real data brings: duplicated records, features on wildly different scales, and thresholds that trade one error for another. Each lesson here runs on a real dataset, and each algorithm is written out and then checked against a trusted implementation, so what is taught is shown to be correct.

findings.label: Datasets
findings.value: SMS Spam Collection, Combined Cycle Power Plant

phases.gate_notes: Four lessons, two datasets and three reference checks fixed before building.

phases.name: data_understanding
phases.title: 2. Data Understanding
phases.objective: Find what in each dataset would mislead a naive lesson.
phases.narrative:
**SMS.** 5,574 messages, 13.4% spam. 403 are exact copies of an earlier message, and copies are disproportionately spam (26% of duplicated messages, against 13.4% overall): the same promotion sent to many people.

**Power plant.** 9,568 hourly readings. Ambient pressure averages 1,013 mbar while temperature averages 19.7 °C, so unscaled features differ by two orders of magnitude.

phases.name: data_preparation
phases.title: 3. Data Preparation
phases.objective: Split so that no message is tested on after being trained on.
phases.narrative:
Messages are deduplicated before an 80/20 stratified split, leaving 4,136 to train and 1,035 to test, with no text in both.

Measured over 20 splits: when duplicates are kept, 10.5% of test messages already appear in training, and Naive Bayes recall is 92.8% against 91.7% when messages are deduplicated first.

findings.label: Test messages seen in training, duplicates kept

phases.gate_notes: Executed assertion: no message text in both splits.

phases.name: modeling
phases.title: 4. Modeling
phases.objective: Write out each algorithm and check it against a trusted implementation.
phases.narrative: **Naive Bayes** is written out with add-one smoothing; its spam probabilities match scikit-learn's to within 2e-14. **Gradient descent** on scaled power-plant features reaches the least-squares coefficients to a relative difference of 1e-16. **Backpropagation** in a 4-8-1 tanh network matches finite differences to 1e-07 over all 49 parameters.

phases.name: evaluation
phases.title: 5. Evaluation
phases.objective: Report what each lesson's analysis actually found.
phases.narrative:
**Spam.** Logistic regression, TF-IDF has the highest average precision, 0.973; Naive Bayes reaches 0.965 with recall 91.6% at a 0.5 threshold.

**Scaling.** Gradient descent is stable only below a learning rate of 0.410 on scaled features and 9.7e-07 on raw ones. After 500 steps, scaled features at learning rate 0.1 reach a training MSE of 20.89; raw features, at just under their own limit, reach 177.8. The exact minimum is 20.89.

**Networks.** The trained network's test RMSE is 4.13 MW against 4.50 MW for linear least squares and 17.03 MW for predicting the mean.

phases.name: deployment
phases.title: 6. Deployment
phases.objective: Serve the lessons live from the checked implementations.
phases.narrative: The API loads the trained Naive Bayes and network and imports ml/lessons.py, so classifying a typed message, moving a threshold, rerunning gradient descent at a new learning rate, or stepping through backpropagation all run the checked code.
phases.gate_notes: Interactive views call the same functions the checks covered.
